name: toolsmith
description: Guides an agent to forge narrow, single-purpose, user-approvable scripts instead of hand-assembling broad escape-hatch commands (gh api, raw curl, aws/gcloud/kubectl).

interface.shortDescription: Forge narrow, allowlistable scripts instead of hand-rolling broad escape-hatch commands; hooks redirect to approved tools and hash-pin them.
interface.longDescription: Broad commands like gh api, raw curl, aws, or kubectl are painful to allowlist — granting them wholesale over-empowers the agent, so they stay gated and every use costs a manual approval. Toolsmith's answer is to forge a narrow tool: a single-purpose script the user proofreads once and allowlists forever. A PreToolUse hook redirects a watched command to an already-approved script when one covers it, and hard-blocks any registered script that is unapproved or whose contents changed since approval (sha256-pinned). A PostToolUse hook logs Bash usage so the analyze command can mine it for tools worth building. The approve command runs the proofread-then-allowlist handshake, coupling each allowlist grant to one reviewed script version.
capabilities: PreToolUse redirect from broad watched commands to an approved covering tool
sha256 hash-pinning that blocks any approved script edited after approval
PostToolUse Bash history logging (bounded, gitignored) for later analysis
Commands to analyze history, run the approval handshake, and list registry status
interface.defaultPrompt: Analyze my recent broad command usage and propose narrow tools worth building.
